newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FOCUS - EU to tell Belgium to reclaim illegal aid.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - EU to tell Belgium to reclaim illegal aid.

text.p: The Belgian government must reclaim 11.4 billion Belgian francs ($353.6 million) of illegal state aid it paid to exporting companies, European Union Competition Commissioner Karel van Miert said on Tuesday.
"Tomorrow the European Commission will formally decide that Maribel II and Maribel III have broken EU rules on state aid," Van Miert told a news conference.
"This is illegal help that must be reclaimed," he said, adding that it totalled 11.4 billion francs.

Under the Maribel II and Maribel III schemes which ran from 1993 to mid-1996, labour-intensive Belgian firms facing foreign competition got exemptions on social security contributions ranging from 25,000 to 37,200 francs per year per worker.
Van Miert said that an updated Maribel IV scheme, in effect since June, also failed to comply with EU state aid rules.

The Commissioner -- a Belgian -- said that as small firms with less than 20 employees would fall below the regulatory threshold of 100,000 European currency units (four million Belgian francs) over a three-year period, the full amount of aid that was paid out might not be reclaimed.
"(Aid to these small firms) would have no influence on intra-Community trade," he said.

Van Miert declined to say which individual companies would be most affected, but indicated that large firms would have to repay more than 75,000 francs per worker. He declined to say by when the aid would have to be repaid.
The Belgian government now has two months in which to reply to the European Commission's ruling, Van Miert said.
Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene's spokeswoman declined comment. "We will wait for the formal decision by the European Commission on Wednesday, then we will react," she said.
Van Miert said the European Union had no objection to general measures to fight unemployment but that they could not be targeted at exporting firms only.
Asked if the Commission would take Belgium to the European Court of Justice if the government did not comply, van Miert said: "Before going to court we will see how the Belgian government reacts".

The Belgian Employers Federation FEB/VBO said in a statement that scrapping the Maribel schemes would hurt Belgian companies' competitive position, and called for a general cut in social security contributions.
"The scrapping of Maribel II and III would handicap us vis-a-vis (companies in) the neighbouring countries," it said. ($1=32.24 Belgian Franc)
